title: refactor(ci): consolidate node workflows, bump actions, and deps hygiene
author: Ava Chen
description:
Background: Over the last 18 months CI workflows proliferated (separate lint/test/release workflows per language, many ad-hoc caching steps, and multiple GitHub Action versions). This caused flakiness, duplicated maintenance, and slow iteration on infra changes. This PR consolidates Node/TS build/test/lint/release workflows into a smaller set with shared reusable steps, bumps official actions to recommended versions, and cleans up obsolete job matrices and caches.

What this PR does (high level):
- Consolidates three legacy Node workflows into two unified workflows: node-lint-test.yml and node-release.yml.
- Standardizes on Node 20 for all pipelines where Node is required; still allows Node 18 compatibility matrix for legacy packages with documented opt-in.
- Bumps commonly used GH Actions (checkout, setup-node, cache, upload-artifact) to their latest stable minor versions to address CVEs and perf regressions.
- Introduces a centralized reusable workflow for caching and build matrix to reduce duplication and cache key mismatches.
- Removes deprecated custom bash wrappers and replaces with lightweight JS action steps for clearer logs and retry semantics.
- Adds more granular cache keys (platform + pnpm-lock) to reduce cache corruption and improve hit rates.
- Adds gating check in release workflow to prevent automatic publish if canary/e2e failed.

Motivation and context:
- Related Linear tickets: ENG-1423 (CI reliability), ENG-1580 (release automation hardening).
- Incident SUP-2991 highlighted a flaky publish flow caused by inconsistent node versions between lint and release runners.

Testing done:
- Local dry-run using act for key job paths, validated composite action inputs.
- Branch CI run: full lint + unit + integration + release-checks passed after two iterations (first run failed due to cache-key collision; fixed by switching to pnpm-lock hash + runner-arch).
- Small subset of downstream repos (redwood-sdk-typescript, redwood-quickstarts) tested via temporary workflow dispatch; no regressions observed.

Checklist: 
- [x] Consolidate workflows and remove duplicates
- [x] Bump GH Actions versions and test CI end-to-end
- [x] Add explanatory docs to devdocs/ci.md
- [x] Update release automation gating and add a manual confirmation step for major releases

Migration notes / follow-ups:
- Teams owning legacy packages should migrate their package.json engines to Node 20 within next 60 days or opt into the node-legacy compatibility matrix.
- Observability: we will add a Prometheus metric for cache hit rate in a follow-up (ENG-1604).
